title: Ontology design principles we follow
what_this_is: Every principle from Palantir's open ontology docs, plus the places we depart. One register instead of six prose documents, because a principle that is only asserted in prose is not a principle — it is a preference. Each carries a stance and, where one is possible, a machine check that runs in CI.

stances.adopt: Taken as written. No local variant.
stances.adapt: Taken, with a stated change of authority or scope.
stances.refuse: Deliberately not followed. The reason is the interesting part.
stances.guard: An anti-pattern we are not in but could fall into.
stances.open: Not yet decided or not yet reachable.

principles.rule: Model the real world, not the source data. Never map 1:1 from whatever the upstream table happened to look like.
principles.ours: A composition row is a source-system artifact. The object is a food in a matrix, eaten by a host, at a rate.
principles.why_not_checkable: Needs the manifest, which does not exist yet.

principles.rule: Separate identity from observation: the entity is not the measurement.
principles.ours: Q1 does not determine Q2. `Food` and `FoodValue` are different object types — the apple is the entity, 927 compounds from three labs are observations of it.

principles.rule: One instance is coincidence, two is a pattern, three triggers refactoring.
principles.ours: Applied to duplicated ontology artifacts across repos.

principles.rule: Lock the essential properties of core types. Extend via linked types, new interface implementations or property namespaces — never by editing the core.
principles.ours: The governance model FDP-1 needs anyway: consumers pin a version, and a public ontology cannot reshape a type underneath them.

principles.rule: Interfaces around capabilities, not taxonomy (Inspectable, Schedulable, Billable).
principles.ours: Gradeable, Declarable, Fenced, Refusable. A workflow written against Gradeable runs over a food value, a score, a study record and a claim without knowing which it has.

principles.rule: A multi-field, semantically related value is a struct.
principles.ours: An FDP-1 value: value + unit + source + method + source_ref + retrieved.

principles.rule: A struct that should behave like a simple value designates a main field.
principles.ours: `Declared[T]` — `.value()` is the main field, provenance rides along.

principles.rule: Common properties or actions across types become an interface.
principles.ours: Gradeable / Declarable / Fenced / Refusable.

principles.rule: A relationship carrying metadata is an object-backed link.
principles.ours: SURFACE_CLAIM's join — claim to study, carrying verb class and verdict. The join IS the object.

principles.rule: A value computed from linked objects is a derived property. Never store it.
principles.ours: The weakest-link grade. A stored grade is a grade that can drift from its inputs.

principles.rule: A value from stable pipeline inputs is a pipeline transform, not a derived property.
principles.ours: Register builds (`make registers`), the crosswalk normalizer, the vocabulary builder.

principles.rule: Object types are singular concrete nouns.
principles.ours: Food, Nutrient, Study, Claim, Host, Law, Exposure.

principles.rule: Do not encode the type in the property name (`nameStr`, `dateDt`).
principles.ours: Register fields follow this already.
principles.why_not_checkable: Broad convention; no cheap complete check.

principles.rule: One date convention across the ontology.
principles.ours: ISO 8601 everywhere; `as_of` on registers, `retrieved` on FDP-1 values.

principles.rule: Qualify ambiguous terms specifically rather than reusing a vague one.
principles.ours: The fix for the layer collision. THE OPEN BLOCKER.

principles.rule: Same entity, separate types per source system.
principles.ours: aca.ttl and claim-shape.ttl exist in two places as byte-identical mirrors with no declared owner. The crosswalk pair is NOT this — it is a declared derivation.

principles.rule: Vague or overloaded names cause cross-team confusion from varied interpretations.
principles.ours: PRESENT, and the worst one. 'Layer' means the OBO causal spine L1-L5 and the standardization stack L0-L9. Also 'unit' and 'grade' vs 'tier'.

principles.rule: One type covering distinct entities.
principles.ours: Risk that Food absorbs raw ingredient, branded product, recipe and meal at once.
principles.why_not_checkable: Needs the manifest. Guard it there.

principles.rule: Historical versions modelled as separate objects.
principles.ours: Versioning is on the record (`*.v1.json` + `as_of`, Zenodo concept + version DOIs), not modelled as separate objects.

principles.rule: Separate versions of a shared entity per team.
principles.ours: NOT the anti-pattern. STUDY_UNIT and MI-Nutrition share two properties and are orthogonal axes (licenses vs discloses), not rival copies. Recorded because the resemblance is misleading.
principles.why_not_checkable: Settled by field comparison, not by a standing check.

principles.rule: ETL metadata should not become properties.
principles.ours: REFUSED. Here provenance IS business data — it is what licenses the claim. A naive application of this would strip exactly the fields the book exists to argue for.

principles.rule: Many single-property actions instead of cohesive ones.
principles.ours: Validators are cohesive (validate_fdp, validate_mi_nutrition).

principles.rule: One tool applied to every problem.
principles.ours: No evidence either way yet. Recorded rather than guessed.
principles.why_not_checkable: Not assessable without the manifest; refusing to fake a verdict.

principles.rule: Every operational decision comprises Data, Logic, Action and Security.
principles.ours: Data = registers, packets, crosswalk, corpus. Logic = 47 laws / 9 gates / 38 bounds. Action = validators and Declared[T] refusals.

principles.rule: The fourth component is Security — does policy permit this decision?
principles.ours: ADAPTED to Provenance — is this decision LICENSED BY EVIDENCE? Same shape, different authority. Published evidence has no access-control problem, and a claim with perfect access control and no method is still worthless.
principles.why_not_checkable: A modelling stance, not a testable state.

principles.rule: Dataset->object type, row->object, column->property, field->property value, join->link type.
principles.ours: Exact until row four. 'Field -> property value' ASSUMES A FIELD HAS A VALUE. 20,983 of our 33,564 crosswalk cells do not. We extend with a third state.

principles.rule: (Our extension.) A property value is a value, NONE (checked, none exists), or OPEN (nobody looked). Never Optional[T].
principles.ours: Declared[T]. The whole reason the SDK is worth building rather than wrapping.

principles.rule: Every object type shows its dependents: an ontology has consumers and a type change breaks them.
principles.ours: Generated by ontology_inventory.py. Not having this is what let the crosswalk sit blocked for a month.

principles.rule: Near-real-time usage and monitoring rules per type and per function.
principles.ours: PARTIAL and hand-measured once (2026-08-24: two phrases moved a published pooled effect 0.78 to 0.75). Nothing recomputes it. This is the valuable missing piece.
principles.why_not_checkable: Not built. Declared as the gap rather than claimed.

principles.rule: Propose an ontology change on a branch without breaking live readers.
principles.ours: We have ratchets, not branches. A ratchet makes a change fail loudly; it does not let you see the consequence before committing.

principles.rule: Object views are a presentation layer, not a structural component.
principles.ours: The evidence hub is NOT part of this ontology and must not be modelled into it. It renders registers; it does not define them.

principles.rule: Build reasonably now with clear improvement paths rather than blocking on perfection. Defend critical invariants: naming quality, semantic clarity and security design are hard to fix retroactively.
principles.ours: Our hard-to-fix-later invariants are NAMING (the layer collision), IDENTITY (one canonical crosswalk) and DECLAREDNESS (OPEN never collapsing to null). Two of three are now gated.
principles.why_not_checkable: A meta-rule about the other rules.
